topics.topic: Outcome precedence when resource exhaustion is followed by unconfirmed cleanup
questions: When output handling records a memory or output resource hit but cleanup cannot be confirmed, must the earlier resource_exhausted outcome win, or must cleanup_failed override it with crashed?

quotes: a MemoryError while it pre-counts, encodes or sends the outputs is a memory hit too, so an output too large to send concludes resource_exhausted rather than crashed, an unconfirmed cleanup still deciding crashed with cleanup_failed as its note says.
when either cannot be confirmed the outputs are discarded and the result is outcome crashed with detail_code cleanup_failed of = models.DetailCode;
judgement.why: Unconfirmed cleanup overrides the earlier resource hit and produces crashed with cleanup_failed.

topics.topic: Whether flow input endpoints count as already successfully concluded, allowing advance_run to deliver guarded must edges immediately
questions: Must edges from flow inputs be delivered immediately, or remain neither enabled nor disabled because their empty-string source endpoint never concludes? One passage must change or explicitly define a flow input endpoint as already concluded succeeded.

quotes: The next node is the ready node with the smallest node_id; a node is ready when every input port holds its value: flow inputs delivered along every edge from them — a flow input or flow output endpoint is the node whose node_id is the empty string (A05 rule 2), never the flow_id —, constants to their port — a FlowConstant's value is the value_id of the StoredValue composition wrote, delivered as a StoredValuesRef naming it, published again by nothing —, and outputs of a concluded succeeded node along every edge whose guard is absent or whose guard port value equals the guard value as canonical JSON text.
judgement.why: The readiness rule separately requires flow inputs to be delivered along every edge from them, while the concluded-source guard condition applies to outputs of nodes.
